A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same noise-scheduling research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet-256 and ImageNet-512 experiments, including schedule comparisons, convergence results, prediction-target evaluations and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original timestep-interval tests, sampling-versus-weighting comparisons, CelebA and CC12M results, and generated-image comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix A.3 introduces Cosine-Ply, which applies a polynomial timestep-sampling transformation before the cosine schedule; A.6 also evaluates its loss-weighting variant. These extend the existing scheduling framework. The original Laplace implementation remains identical.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates class-conditional ImageNet generation at two resolutions. v2 additionally evaluates unconditional face generation on CelebA in 64×64 pixel space and text-conditioned generation on CC12M at 256×256, substantially broadening domains, conditioning requirements and data representations.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in Table 3 remains unchanged. New appendix comparisons introduce Cosine-Ply against Laplace and evaluate Cosine-Ply as a loss weight alongside the retained weighting baselines. Logit-normal flow matching receives analytical discussion, not a newly reported empirical baseline evaluation.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 adds a distinct protocol: train for one million iterations, fine-tune separately within four timestep bins for 140,000 iterations, and selectively substitute checkpoints during inference. A.7 adds a specified CelebA model configuration and a 200,000-iteration CC12M setup. The original ImageNet evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled tests of which timestep intervals benefit from fine-tuning, a direct comparison of the same sampling distribution used as scheduling versus loss weighting, and matched-initial-noise visual case studies across training checkpoints. These substantially extend v1's prediction-target, resolution and schedule-parameter analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, empirical variability or statistical significance tests. The distributional mean and variance derived in A.4 are theoretical properties, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 3–7 are numerically unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results. Table 9 reports FID-10K of 7.98 for Cosine-Ply versus 8.88 as a loss weight. New Laplace-versus-cosine results include 6.58359 versus 7.93795 on CelebA at 150,000 iterations and 54.3492 versus 58.3619 on CC12M at 200,000 iterations. Additional convergence, interval and visual findings are also reported.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly defines the normalized polynomial timestep distribution, its sampling transformation and its induced log-SNR density. A.4 derives that logit-normal timestep sampling in flow matching induces a normal log-SNR distribution with mean -2µ and variance 4σ². These extend the mathematical analysis beyond the retained scheduling identities.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: noise scheduling corresponds to importance sampling, concentrating computation near log SNR = 0 improves training efficiency, and Laplace benefits ImageNet generation across prediction targets. The new contribution list makes existing claims explicit without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that concentration around intermediate noise levels matters more than the precise schedule family, connects logit-normal flow sampling to this principle, and discusses generalization across conditioning regimes. It also explicitly limits the study's objective to fixed-budget efficiency rather than XL-scale or state-of-the-art performance.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies patch size, conditioning details, continuous implementation and γ = 5 for the weighting baselines. It also supplies CelebA architecture and CC12M preprocessing, CLIP-conditioning and training details. The Laplace code is unchanged; the earlier Appendix B sampling instructions are relocated into Section 2.4.

R1.justification: v2 expands background citations and discussion, including Ernie-ViLG 2.0, additional video/3D diffusion work, and Movie Gen in the logit-normal analysis. It elaborates connections to MM-DiT, HDiT and prior noise schedules while retaining the same central research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction and method explanation undergo extensive rewriting, including an explicit contribution list and expanded probability-based narrative. The ablation discussion is expanded, sampling instructions move into the main text, and the appendix is reorganized into eight subsections. These changes exceed simple renumbering or insertion of results.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–11 and Figures 4–8, including density plots, interval comparisons, weighting curves and generated-image grids. Figure 2 expands from one convergence panel to two, Figure 3's legend is rearranged, and Table 1 is reformatted. The visual presentation changes substantially despite retained main-table values.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's reliance on ImageNet and indirect comparisons between sampling and weighting. The new CelebA/CC12M evaluations and controlled interval and sampling-versus-weighting tests strengthen generalizability and support for the central argument. Added derivations and implementation disclosures improve assessability. Repeated-run uncertainty remains absent, and Table 8 inconsistently labels the Laplace parameter in its caption, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantive gains.
